rationale: Two things are submitted together: the knowledge use that last turn's answer could not record because the entry was created in the same batch, and a probe that separates the two gates the previous negative result left entangled. With pre-vote disabled an isolated voter does raise its term, so the adverse history the earlier run could not construct now exists; the local dry run, explicitly not retained evidence, shows the candidacy forming in every trial and still no overlap, which would put the uniform-case separation on the peers' known-leader refusal and their timers rather than on pre-vote.

investigations.question: With pre-vote disabled so that an isolated voter does raise its term, does the uniform-case separation still hold, or does the known-leader gate alone fail to keep the cut-off leader's confirmation from overlapping a competing election?
investigations.hypothesis: Pre-vote is an additional gate rather than the necessary one: even with a higher-term candidate campaigning, a peer that still has the leader in view refuses the vote request before comparing terms, and that view lapses no earlier than the peer's own heartbeat timer, which with shared settings is at least the leader's lease - so the separation should survive.
investigations.discriminator: Repeat the adverse construction with PreVoteDisabled set on every node, and record both whether a higher-term candidacy forms (which the previous run could not produce) and whether any confirmation follows a competing leader. A formed candidacy with no overlap puts the separation on the known-leader gate; a formed candidacy with an overlap would extend the defect to clusters that disable pre-vote.

knowledge.statement: Two gates keep an isolated voter from displacing a leader whose lease is still running when every node shares its timer settings. A node that knows a leader refuses a vote request from any other candidate before it compares terms, so a candidate cannot collect the vote of a peer that still has the leader in view; and with pre-vote enabled the candidate does not raise its term at all while it cannot assemble a majority, because runCandidate's pre-vote phase keeps the node at its current term and only elects for real after the pre-vote is won. Both gates are released by the same event - a peer losing the leader from view when its own heartbeat timer expires - and that timer is reset by the same leader whose lease is expiring, so with shared settings the lease expires no later than the earliest moment at which a vote could be granted.
knowledge.conditions: Pre-vote enabled (the captured default), sending nodes sharing their timer settings, the candidate isolated from the leader and from a majority of voters, and ValidateConfig's per-node relation LeaderLeaseTimeout <= HeartbeatTimeout <= ElectionTimeout holding on every node.

knowledge.assertion: The two gates named there are what the twenty adverse trials exercised together; the run could not attribute the separation to either alone.

interpretations.rationale: Same account as the previous revision of this question, with the knowledge entry it relies on recorded at its exact revision and the limitation about the two gates stated in the entry text itself. The executed comparison predicted an overlap once a voter was already campaigning before the leader's isolation; it came back violated and complete with all twenty adverse trials as valid witnesses, and the campaigner's recorded state and term (Candidate at the leader's own term in every trial) show that pre-vote prevented a higher-term candidacy from forming at all, so the separation was confirmed but its attribution was left to the combination. Nothing else changes: the confirmations ended at the leader's lease in every trial, no competing leader appeared during the window, and the two plain controls behaved the same way.
counterevidence: The attribution limitation is the substance of the entry as recorded: with pre-vote on, the run cannot tell whether the peers' known-leader refusal alone would also have kept the separation.
Pre-vote is what the captured default enables; a cluster configured without it was not measured in this run.
No application read is served, so the measurement is the coexistence of a confirmation with a competing leader rather than a delivered value.
limitations: One cluster shape and one set of identical 50ms settings, in one process with in-memory transports.
The adverse history reaches only as far as isolating one voter for up to three seconds.
A separate probe is submitted to test the pre-vote-disabled configuration that would separate the gates.

scope.description: Twelve trials on hand-built four-node clusters whose nodes all share 50ms settings and all have PreVoteDisabled set: one voter is isolated first and left to campaign, which with pre-vote off raises its term, and only then are the leader and the nonvoter isolated from the two remaining voters while the leader's verifications are polled and the two voters watched for a leader.
assumptions: PreVoteDisabled is a public configuration field, so disabling pre-vote is a supported deployment choice rather than an artificial one; it is the configuration that separates the two gates the earlier run could not distinguish.
The candidate's term is recorded before and after the isolation so the run shows whether a higher-term candidacy formed.
Verification is driven through the same channel the exported API uses; a competing leader is detected by reading the two isolated nodes' states.
The dry run is native feedback only; the retained execution is what will be interpreted.
excluded: No on-disk store, no network transport, no multi-process execution.
Only the uniform configuration with pre-vote off is exercised here.

parameters.trials: 12 adverse trials with pre-vote disabled (trial ids 0-11)
parameters.recorded_operands: adverse, preexisting_candidate, campaigner_state, campaigner_term, leader_term, polls, confirmations, last_confirmation_ms, first_peer_leader_ms, confirmations_after_peer_leader, confirmation_after_peer_leader, leader_stepped_down

comparisons.description: Prediction under test: with pre-vote disabled and a higher-term candidacy alive, at least one confirmation follows a competing leader. Trials that fail it are witnesses that the known-leader gate and the timers keep the separation without pre-vote.

experiment.prefix: The harness is the adverse-phase probe with one change: every node's Config has PreVoteDisabled set, and only the twelve adverse trials run. Each trial builds four nodes by hand with identical settings, waits for a leader, forces leadership onto node 0, demotes node 3 to nonvoter, records a baseline confirmation and one applied command, isolates node 1 and waits up to three seconds for it to report Candidate with a term above the leader's, then isolates the leader and the nonvoter from both remaining voters and polls the verification path every 2ms while watching those voters for a leader, emitting a summary event per trial with the counts, the campaigner's state and term, the leader's term and whether any confirmation followed a competing leader.
